keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's only County of Portugal row starts in 1139, but the county under Henry and Theresa and then Afonso Henriques existed from 1096. The page gives no boundary before 1139 (page silent on the Mondego, Tui and the Almoravid frontier), so Cliopatria's 1139 shape is carried back unchanged; unverified: page budget. The shape stops short of Santarém, which 'the Muslims conquered' in 1111 (Santarem 25 km radius has no cell in it).

correction.text: the shape unchanged: 'much of the current Portuguese territory between the Minho River and the Tagus River'; it holds 1139-1143, when the county ends and Portugal is 'recognized... as a fully independent kingdom' (Treaty of Zamora); 1144-1146 belong to the kingdom of Portugal

keyframe_review.note: 165 cells, 46,123 km2, bbox 39.58-42.11 N, 9.03-6.25 W (Viana do Castelo to Castelo Branco). The page's infobox has no area (page silent), so no comparison; the extent 'between the Minho and the Tagus' agrees. Only the years change: the County page and Afonso I page end the county at Ourique/Zamora (1139-1143) while Cliopatria keeps 'County of Portugal' to 1146 and starts its Kingdom of Portugal row in 1147, the year Santarém (15 May) and Lisbon were taken. The kingdom-of-portugal dossier must draw this same shape for 1144-1146 or those years have no state.

ledger.note: 1096: Alfonso VI grants Portugal and Coimbra to Henry of Burgundy. 'Alfonso VI separated Portugal and Coimbra from Galicia and granted them to Henry of Burgundy, who was married to Theresa' (County of Portugal page); Henry 'chose Guimarães as the base' that year. The page gives the lands, not a boundary; the Cliopatria 1139 shape stands in for them. The page's older dates (868 Vímara Peres, 1093 Raymond of Burgundy as count of Galicia including Portugal to Coimbra) belong to the Galician and Leonese dossiers.

region.text: Portugal and Coimbra, separated from Galicia and granted to Henry of Burgundy

ledger.note: 1131: the seat moves from Guimarães to Coimbra. The infobox gives 'Guimarães (868-1131) Coimbra (1131-1139)'. The Afonso I page does not mention the move (it says only that Theresa died in 1131).

1139 (25 July): after the victory at Ourique Afonso Henriques is acclaimed King of the Portuguese. 'On 25 July 1139, he obtained an overwhelming victory in the Battle of Ourique' and was 'straight after... proclaimed King of the Portuguese by his soldiers'; 'the first reference to his royal title dates from 1140' (Afonso I page). The County page: 'Battle of Ourique: 1139', and he had used the title Prince from 6 April 1129. The land does not change; the state is a kingdom in all but recognition.

1143: Leon recognises Portugal as independent and the county ends in the Kingdom of Portugal. The Treaty of Zamora (1143) 'established peace between the cousins' and recognised Portugal as 'a fully independent kingdom' (Afonso I page); the County page gives 1143 as the end point ('recognized by the Kingdom of León in 1143'), with the infobox 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Portugal'. The day (5 October) is not on either page.

region.text: the whole shape of 1139-1143, which passes to the Kingdom of Portugal

wars.name: Battle of São Mamede
wars.outcome: 'In 1128, near Guimarães at the Battle of São Mamede', Afonso's forces defeated his mother Theresa's and Fernando Pérez de Traba's troops; Afonso 'exiled his mother to Galicia, and took over rule of the County of Portucale'.
wars.note: A struggle for the county's rulership (rule 5 on the map) rather than for land; the page gives no day.

wars.name: Battle of Ourique
wars.outcome: 'On 25 July 1139, he obtained an overwhelming victory in the Battle of Ourique'; the enemy is 'the Moors' on the page (Almoravids by identification); the page does not place the battle or name land won.
wars.note: Afonso was proclaimed king afterwards; no territory is attached to the battle on the pages opened.

wars.name: Portuguese-Leonese conflict ended by the Treaty of Zamora
wars.outcome: 'the Treaty of Zamora (1143) established peace between the cousins' and recognised Portugal as 'a fully independent kingdom'.
wars.note: Fighting 1137-1143 (Cerneja, Valdevez) is not dated on either page; only the 1143 treaty year is given. Afonso's conquests in Galicia north of the Minho (surrendered after Badajoz, 1169) are undated and outside the Cliopatria shape.

certainty.note: A frontier county between Galicia, Leon and the Almoravid south; no treaty or survey line before the Treaty of Zamora (1143), which names none.

notes:
County of Portugal is one Cliopatria row of one shape, 1139-1146 (46,123 km2: bbox 39.58-42.11 N, Viana do Castelo to Castelo Branco). Both pages end the county in 1139-1143 (Ourique, Zamora), while Cliopatria keeps the label to 1146 and starts its Kingdom of Portugal in 1147; this dossier ends the county in 1143 and starts it in 1096, when Alfonso VI granted 'Portugal and Coimbra' to Henry of Burgundy (the page's 868 date for Vímara Peres' earlier vassal county, and 1093, belong to Galicia/Leon). The kingdom-of-portugal dossier of another group has to carry the shape for 1144-1146 (or start in 1139/1143).
Not settled (pages silent): the county's boundary before 1139 (Mondego, Tui, Limia, the Almoravid frontier); the 1111 loss of Santarém, which the County page gives as 'the Muslims conquered Santarém' without saying whom it belonged to (the Cliopatria shape already stops short of it); the 1137-1140 war with Alfonso VII (Cerneja, Valdevez, any Galician land); the day of the Treaty of Zamora; Afonso's conquests north of the Minho, surrendered after Badajoz in 1169 (Afonso I page). The 1121 subservience of Theresa to Leon is a vassalage that kingdom-of-leon (another group) should carry as vassal_start counterpart county-of-portugal. Rulers strip omitted (page budget). Counterparts that need dossiers from other groups: kingdom-of-galicia, kingdom-of-leon, almoravid-dynasty (written), kingdom-of-portugal (eu-12 part).
Page budget (1-2): County of Portugal, Afonso I of Portugal.
